editorial.headline: Book Publishing: Nationally Open, but Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Book publishing can be fully foreign-owned nationally, yet Bali’s permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration for this activity across the island.
editorial.body:
Book publishing covers the act of bringing books into publication in its many possible forms. Its scope includes books, brochures and similar publications; dictionaries and encyclopaedias; atlases, maps and charts; electronic books and audiobooks; and comic books and graphic novels. The definition is deliberately format-neutral: print, electronic, digital, analogue and other forms of book publication all sit within the activity. For an enterprise built around publishing books rather than a single delivery format, this is the relevant frame.

The activity is open to businesses at Micro, Small, Medium and Large scale. Nationally, it is open to PMA, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. That makes the national position unusually direct: a foreign investor may hold the full permitted stake in a book-publishing business under this activity. The record identifies the national basis as Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali is the decisive exception. In Bali today, this activity cannot be registered as PMA by a foreigner. At the Large scale, OSS assigns Low or Medium-Low risk across every scope within the activity, placing it inside Bali’s moratorium. The provincial rule blocks PMA for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities, island-wide and permanently. For book publishing, the result is not a reduced foreign-ownership ceiling or a local-partnership condition: it is a block on PMA registration in Bali.

That distinction matters because the national permission remains real, but it does not override the Bali position. A founder considering this activity therefore has to read the two layers together: national rules allow up to full foreign ownership, while Bali’s risk-based moratorium prevents a PMA registration for the activity on the island. The commercial shape of the publishing business—whether centred on printed books, e-books, audio editions, reference works, maps or graphic novels—does not change the stated Bali outcome, because the record applies the Low or Medium-Low classification across every scope.
editorial.pullQuote: Nationally, book publishing is open to 100% foreign ownership; in Bali, PMA registration is blocked across the island.
